external_input_scope: Grauert upper semicontinuity and constant-dimension base change; Cartan B/Leray for the complex-line base are standard classical inputs. Existing marked conjugacy, Hopf argument, note77 and note97 surface lemma reused.
corrigendum_scope: The false closedness assertion for the general base-change failure set in Section7 Satz2 is not used. Closed upper level sets of cohomology dimension come instead from Satz3. Constant-dimension Satz5 is used only over the smooth line.
new_proof_interfaces: Fast Lefschetz flux pairing has slow kernel and nondegenerate fast block; no complex period rank lifting is asserted.
Two real generators of the same holomorphic flow have independent fast rotations by the fast pairing, then exact constant displacement by L1 scaling.
Full right displacement is Gamma-periodic, lies in the abelian expanding subgroup, and has a residual square-root bound; that bound is not treated as vanishing.
Nondegenerate fast displacement makes the C action proper on the fast-primary covering without equicontinuity on compact X.
A compact invariant continuous section of the quotient at zero makes the actual derivative quotient Anosov.
A smooth principal C section gives one closed smooth two-form on Q, hence constant reduced symplectic periods; it is not declared holomorphic.
Dense deck translations plus cohomology upper semicontinuity force constant Hodge numbers.
The actual holomorphic torsor class obeys G* kappa = lambda^2 kappa. If its restriction vanishes at zero, dense translates and base change make it vanish globally.
A holomorphic section produces a closed holomorphic two-form on Q and a complete horizontal characteristic line, hence an actual holomorphic symplectic product.
Properness descends to the complex two-dimensional fast quotient because the other factor Y is compact; the resulting aspherical Z4 complex surface is a torus by the existing surface lemma.
If W_X has dimension one, kappa_0 must be nonzero, Y has W_Y=0, and H1(Y,O) has a new fast eigenclass outside H1(Y,C), so h01>=9.
